title: UAS (Drone) Operations Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of UAS/drone regulations, airspace access, and safe operations from AIM Chapter 11

questions.question: What weight limit defines a small UAS (sUAS) under Part 107?
questions.explanation: Part 107 applies to small UAS weighing less than 55 pounds. UAS 55 pounds or more require different authorization (Part 91 with COA or exemption).

questions.question: What is the maximum altitude for sUAS operations in Class G airspace under Part 107?
questions.explanation: Part 107 sUAS operations are limited to 400 feet AGL in Class G airspace, or within 400 feet of a structure if flying over it.

questions.question: What is LAANC?
options: Low Altitude Authorization and Notification Capability
Limited Airspace Access for Non-Commercial aircraft
Landing Area Authorization for National Coverage
questions.explanation: LAANC (Low Altitude Authorization and Notification Capability) automates the application and approval process for UAS airspace authorizations in controlled airspace.

questions.question: What test must recreational drone flyers pass?
questions.explanation: Recreational flyers must pass TRUST (The Recreational UAS Safety Test), an online safety test with no minimum age requirement.

questions.question: At what weight must a recreational UAS be registered?
questions.explanation: Recreational UAS weighing more than 0.55 pounds (250 grams) must be registered with the FAA. Part 107 UAS must be registered regardless of weight.

questions.question: What is required for Part 107 operations in controlled airspace?
options: Prior authorization from ATC via LAANC or DroneZone
questions.explanation: Part 107 operations in Class B, C, D, or surface E airspace require prior ATC authorization via LAANC (for UASFM altitudes) or DroneZone (for further coordination).

questions.question: What is Remote Identification (RID)?
options: The ability of a UAS in flight to broadcast identification and location information
questions.explanation: Remote ID enables a UAS in flight to broadcast identification and location data receivable by others, helping FAA and law enforcement identify operators.

questions.question: What is a FRIA?
questions.explanation: FRIA (FAA-Recognized Identification Area) is a geographic area where UAS can operate without Remote ID, maintaining visual line of sight.

questions.question: What minimum age is required for a Part 107 remote pilot certificate?
questions.explanation: To obtain a Part 107 remote pilot certificate, applicants must be at least 16 years old and able to speak and understand English.

questions.question: What is the UASFM?
questions.explanation: UASFM (UAS Facility Map) shows maximum altitudes for UAS operations that can be approved via LAANC without further coordination with ATC.

questions.question: Can Part 107 operators fly at night?
options: Yes, with proper training and anti-collision lighting
questions.explanation: Part 107 allows night operations with initial pilot training and anti-collision lighting visible for 3 statute miles. No waiver required.

questions.question: What must a Part 107 remote pilot report to the FAA?
options: Accidents causing serious injury or >$500 property damage (other than UAS)
questions.explanation: Part 107 pilots must report accidents causing serious injury, loss of consciousness, or property damage (other than to the UAS) exceeding $500.

questions.question: What does VLOS mean in UAS operations?
questions.explanation: VLOS (Visual Line of Sight) means the remote pilot can see the UAS with unaided vision (except corrective lenses). Required for Part 107 operations unless waived.

questions.question: Who has right-of-way between a manned aircraft and a UAS?
questions.explanation: The UAS operator must always give way to manned aircraft. The pilot retains ultimate responsibility to avoid manned aircraft traffic.

questions.question: What Part regulates commercial drone package delivery BVLOS operations?
questions.explanation: Commercial package delivery BVLOS and interstate HAZMAT transport require Part 135 certification, not Part 107.

questions.question: What is a COA for UAS operations?
questions.explanation: COA (Certificate of Waiver or Authorization) grants public UAS operators and certain civil operators access to specific airspace.

questions.question: What recurrent training is required for Part 107 pilots?
questions.explanation: Part 107 remote pilots must complete recurrent training or pass a recurrent knowledge test every 24 months to exercise certificate privileges.

questions.question: Where can recreational flyers find airspace restrictions?
questions.explanation: The B4UFLY mobile app and LAANC applications help recreational and Part 107 flyers identify airspace restrictions and obtain authorizations.

questions.question: What happens if a recreational flyer violates 49 USC 44809 requirements?
options: The flight is treated as Part 107, potentially with greater penalties
questions.explanation: Failure to adhere to recreational flyer requirements under 49 USC 44809 results in the FAA treating the operation as Part 107, potentially with greater penalties.

questions.question: What is Advanced Air Mobility (AAM)?
options: Emerging sector integrating highly automated aircraft including UAM and cargo delivery
questions.explanation: AAM (Advanced Air Mobility) encompasses emerging technologies including Urban Air Mobility, Regional Air Mobility, cargo delivery, and automated aircraft integration.
